newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Uncertainty in Australia as gold price falls.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Uncertainty in Australia as gold price falls.

text.p: The decline in the gold price below the nervously-watched and keenly traded level of US$380 an ounce has created uncertainty among gold producers over their option strategies, dealers said on Tuesday.
The dealers said put (sell) options priced around US$375.00 an ounce are gaining appeal among some producers who believe the gold market rout is not yet over.
Gold failed to hold above key technical support levels to continue its overnight slide to over 18-month lows, suggesting to some analysts that the precious metal is poised for more tumbles.
Spot gold was quoted at $377.55-$378.05 an ounce at the end of Hong Kong trade on Tuesday compared with a close on Monday in New York of $378.20-$378.60.
"Any strategy that gives the producer some protection to the downside would be welcomed, a bullion dealer for an Australian bank said.
"Aussie producers are not looking too healthy," he added.
A strong Australian currency combined with a weakended international and local gold price has hobbled producers for the time being, another dealer said.
"We're not seeing any business out of Australia, it's been very quiet," he said.
He agreed with other dealers that producers generally were expecting the price to rebound at some point, but acknowledged "that's anyone's guess".
While Australian producers are likely to feel the impact of lower prices on the unhedged portion of their output, it is unlikely to dampen this year's forecast overall production of about 285 tonnes.
"With so much of what producers mine sold forward, what we're seeing in the price is not enough to discourage output," the dealer said.
However, firmer gold lease interest rates for the short dates of around 2.5 percent is discouraging fresh hedging by producers.
Meanwhile, more downward pressure on the gold price could draw out fresh Chinese buying.
"A lot of the Chinese are just sitting back and waiting to see where the rest of the world is going to take the gold market," a dealer for a bank with Chinese clients said.
"The market is very short, so if we get a blowout, who would want sell at say $373.00," he said.
